answers.change_2023_2026: There have been right protections both in 2023 and 2026 and neither the right protection nor the implementation level of these protections has changed

provisions.instrument: Constitución Política de la República de Chile
Ley 20.584 (derechos y deberes de las personas en su atención de salud)

answers.implementation_then_now: In 2023 and in 2026 the law gave the same entitlement: Art. 15 gives resident and irregular foreigners access to health care 'en igualdad de condiciones que los nacionales'. In practice irregular migrants get in through FONASA's provisional identifier (NIP, tramo A). Studies published in 2023–2025 (e.g. Carreño-Calderón et al. 2025, BMC Int J Equity Health, using CASEN 2022 and interviews) document continuing barriers: lack of information, cultural and administrative obstacles, low uptake of programmes. They do not show formal exclusion. I found no documented shift in practice between the two dates. Proposals to restrict benefits for irregular migrants (Amnesty 2025) and a 2026 proposal to make FONASA report irregular users were still bills, and the latter came after the window.

answers.sourcing_note: LeyChile's version list for Ley 21.325 shows the original text (12-02-2022 to 06-08-2023), then amendments by Leyes 21.590, 21.589, 21.610 and 21.655 and a 01-04-2025 version, all inside the window. I read each of the four acts. They amend Arts. 5, 100, 131/134 and Ley 20.430, and none of them touches Art. 15. Today's Art. 15 matches the MRD's 2023 quote word for word. LeyChile prints no amendment note on Ley 20.584 Art. 2 (Art. 1 carries a Ley 21.541 note), and its amendments in the window (21.541, 21.668, 21.746) do not appear to touch Art. 2. I could not read the version history of Constitution Art. 19. Practice evidence is thin and academic.

PMC – Adolescent migrants health barriers in Chile

answers.starting_answer_concern: The protection answer holds: Art. 15 expressly covers irregular migrants on equal terms with nationals. On implementation, documented administrative and informational barriers for irregular migrants, plus low FONASA affiliation of migrant households, suggest 'Usually' is the better fit than 'Usually; Effectively Always'. I kept the starting rating because nothing shows a change.
answers.notes: Art. 15 text (current, identical to the 2023 quote): 'Los extranjeros residentes o en condición migratoria irregular, ya sea en su calidad de titulares o dependientes, tendrán acceso a la salud conforme a los requisitos que la autoridad de salud establezca, en igualdad de condiciones que los nacionales.' I relied on statutes, not court rulings. The 2026 government proposal to make health bodies report irregular migrants came after the window and, as far as I found, had not been enacted.

answers.answer_2023: Yes, but only for certain visa types and migrant statuses (e.g., economic, family, humanitarian, temporary or regular migrants)
answers.answer_2026: Yes, but only for certain visa types and migrant statuses (e.g., economic, family, humanitarian, temporary or regular migrants)
answers.change_2023_2026: There have been right protections both in 2023 and 2026 and neither the right protection nor the implementation level of these protections has changed
answers.implementation_then_now: The law limits equal access to own-housing programmes to foreigners with residencia definitiva. MINVU's DS49 page still requires a foreigner's ID card with permanencia definitiva and the matching certificate, which is a statement of law, not practice. Secondary reports (Faro UDD 2025, seen in search results only, since the PDF could not be read) say foreigners were about 4.6% of DS1 beneficiaries in 2014–2024 and 4.2% of DS49 beneficiaries in 2024. That suggests definitive residents do get subsidies, though below their share of the population. Migrants without definitive residence, including the large population in campamentos, are excluded under the rules. I found no documented shift in practice over the window. A 2024 Consejo de Política Migratoria minute reportedly mentions a planned decree requiring five years of definitive residence, but I could not read it or find the decree.

answers.sourcing_note: Ley 21.325's version list (original text plus Leyes 21.590, 21.589, 21.610, 21.655 and a 01-04-2025 version) was read, and so were the four amending acts. None amends Art. 18, whose current text reads 'Los extranjeros titulares de residencia definitiva gozarán de los mismos derechos en materia de vivienda propia que los nacionales'. I could not open the practice PDFs (Faro UDD br57, the 2024 Consejo minute), so the implementation evidence is weak.

sources_opened.title: LeyChile – Ley 21.325 texto original version and version list

answers.starting_answer_concern: The MRD rated implementation 'Effectively Always; Effectively Never', two non-neighbouring levels that probably mean definitive residents versus everyone else. That pair is not an allowed option. Since the protection answer covers definitive residents only, I record 'Usually' for that group on both dates. This is a translation of the starting rating into the allowed options, not a change. Art. 18 covers only 'vivienda propia' (ownership). Rental subsidies (DS52) are not covered by it, and I did not check their rules.
answers.notes: No ruling or new instrument in the window was found that changes access to public housing for migrants. A reported MINVU plan (2024) for a five-years-of-definitive-residence requirement could not be verified in a decree.
